svg.aria-label: How to write ありがとう: 5 letters, あ, り, が, と, う, one after another
svg.title: Writing ありがとう
svg.desc: 5 letters written one after another: あ, り, が, と, う (japanese). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: あ: KanjiVG, kanji/03042.svg, hiragana あ (U+3042 HIRAGANA LETTER A), three stroke paths kvg:03042-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03042.svg>; り: KanjiVG, kanji/0308a.svg, hiragana り (U+308A HIRAGANA LETTER RI), two stroke paths kvg:0308a-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/0308a.svg>; が: KanjiVG, kanji/0304c.svg, hiragana が (U+304C HIRAGANA LETTER GA), five stroke paths kvg:0304c-s1 to s5 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/0304c.svg>; と: KanjiVG, kanji/03068.svg, hiragana と (U+3068 HIRAGANA LETTER TO), two stroke paths kvg:03068-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03068.svg>; う: KanjiVG, kanji/03046.svg, hiragana う (U+3046 HIRAGANA LETTER U), two stroke paths kvg:03046-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03046.svg>. Source notes on variation: あ: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the bar drawn left to right; s2 starts above the bar and runs down through it; s3 starts at the upper right, cuts down and to the left across the vertical, turns at the lower left without lifting, loops back up and over to the right, rounds the right side of the bowl and finishes low, heading left. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. り: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the left stroke drawn top to bottom, which turns at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 starts at the top of the right stroke, higher than s1, runs down and sweeps away to the lower left. In KanjiVG the two paths do not touch. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. The print glyph has no flick at the foot of the left stroke: a thin stroke leaves it partway down and rises over an arch into the top of the right stroke, the pen's way from one stroke to the next drawn in ink. So the path goes down to the foot of the left stroke, climbs back up the same ink and follows that rise to the top of the arch, where the right stroke begins; in the print glyph, unlike KanjiVG, the two strokes touch there. が: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s3 are か's strokes, the same paths as in its file for か, kanji/0304b.svg; s4 and s5 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. と: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 starts at the top of the short stroke and runs down and to the right, ending on the line s2 will take; s2 starts at the upper right, sweeps down to the left, curves round and runs out to the right along the base. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. In KanjiVG and in the print glyph alike, the short stroke ends on the long one, so the two strokes touch. う: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the short top stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down that the print glyph does not show; s2 starts at the left, rises to the right along the top, rounds the right side and sweeps away to the lower left. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 5 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 5 movements
Letter 2 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Letter 3 of 5 — 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 7 movements
Letter 4 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 5 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03042.svg, hiragana あ (U+3042 HIRAGANA LETTER A), three stroke paths kvg:03042-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 2: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0308a.svg, hiragana り (U+308A HIRAGANA LETTER RI), two stroke paths kvg:0308a-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 3: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0304c.svg, hiragana が (U+304C HIRAGANA LETTER GA), five stroke paths kvg:0304c-s1 to s5 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 4: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03068.svg, hiragana と (U+3068 HIRAGANA LETTER TO), two stroke paths kvg:03068-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 5: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03046.svg, hiragana う (U+3046 HIRAGANA LETTER U), two stroke paths kvg:03046-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
